q: Karl busted the myth that a worm cut in half becomes two worms. What did he say happens if you cut it leaving more neck than tail?
a: The cut-off bit dies, but the rest of the worm gets better
x: The tail end grows itself a new head
Both bits die within the week
The head half forgets which way it was going
f: Karl: "in a way you can cut it in half and it'll survive. But only one half will survive." He later added: "it's not the thing to do either by the way."
ex: So, but what they can do, if you get a worm, right, and you find out which end its head’s at….
…if you, sort of, you’ve got its head there at the left hand side, right, and if you sort of cut it in half…
…but not in half so there’s more of its neck than the tail, if you know what I mean?
The bit you’ve cut off will sort of die, and the rest of the worm will get better, so in a way you can cut it in half and it’ll survive. But only one half will survive.
